title: Flow-Lenia starve-one-daughter IMED replicates on fresh seeds: the food-cut daughter dissolves on 3/3 valid forks (seeds 6, 8, 9) while its sister grows and its fed twin lives; gliders travel 12-13 body lengths and divide to generation 5 (merge/split 0.68-0.85); a 4th fork (seed 7) was invalid because the daughters re-merged
summary: Re-ran world.py and the claim's dfork.py/dplot.py unchanged. Labkit packs on fresh seeds 6 and 7 (t=800): 7 and 9 persistent splits, max generation 5 and 5, merge/split 0.68 and 0.85, max 12.0 and 12.9 body lengths. Starve-one-daughter forks (300 t after the first fresh pair at t>=150): seed 6 (fork t=150, pair 25 px): starved daughter 90.6 -> 0, sister 107 -> 195, the same daughter in the fed twin ends at 78 after growing; seed 8 (t=245, 19 px): starved daughter 105 -> 0 by t~500, while its fed copy grows to ~180; the sister grows 50 -> 323; seed 9 (t=150, 27.5 px): starved daughter 74 -> 0 by t~390, while its fed copy is alive at t=380; the sister grows 90 -> 185 and divides. In each cut run the starved daughter stops gliding and shrinks steadily (forks/df6.png, df8.png, df9.png). Seed 7's fork (t=255, 26.6 px) is invalid: the two bodies fuse within ~35 t, so both trackers end on one body and the comparison means nothing (forks/df7.png).

verdicts.limitation: Genealogy is reticulate (merge/split 0.68-0.85 > 0.5), so D confidence is capped at medium. Founders come from one planted noise patch, so S is not claimed. The nearest-centroid tracker loses or swaps bodies when they touch (seed 7 fork, late fed-twin drops on seeds 8 and 9); the images are the record. The fork search can land on a pair that is about to re-merge, so a valid fork needs checking by eye.
